candidates: When a resolution or lookup function can return three meaningfully distinct outcomes — (1) the property is absent, (2) the property exists but cannot be resolved or processed, and (3) the property exists and was successfully resolved — use a discriminated union return type (e.g. `{ kind: 'missing' } | { kind: 'resolved'; path: T } | { kind: 'unresolved' }`) rather than a nullable. Returning `null`/`undefined` for both 'absent' and 'unresolvable' conflates the two cases, causing callers to incorrectly fall back to lower-precedence defaults (such as a meta-level render) that should only apply when the property is truly absent.
